papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack text pdf/P-117.txt is 'Deep learning-based classification of healthy aging controls, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using fusion of MRI-PET imaging' (Rallabandi & Seetharaman, BSPC 80 (2023) 104312, OASIS), NOT the paper the record means. The record's '99.81% Acc' belongs to Aljalal et al., 'Mild cognitive impairment detection with optimally selected EEG channels based on variational mode decomposition and supervised machine learning', BSPC 87 (2024) 105462 (the summaries.md P-117 block), whose PDF is in the repository at downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809423008959-main.pdf. Both were read in full; the wrong pack PDF reports no 99.81%.
Using a dual-stream attention neural network to characterize mild cognitive impairment based on retinal images (Gao et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 166 (2023) 107411)

what_each_reports.P-117: Aljalal et al. 2024: resting-state 19-channel EEG, 61 participants (29 amnestic MCI, 32 HC) from two public Isfahan (Noor Hospital) datasets, 10-s segments (3660 feature vectors), VMD + entropy features, 10-fold CV over the feature vectors. Binary MCI vs HC accuracy 99.51% with all channels (KNN) and 99.81% with 11 NSGA-II-selected channels (ensemble KNN).
what_each_reports.P-5: DuCAN dual-stream network on fundus photographs + OCT, first dataset 117 patients (29 MCI/58 eyes, 50 CN/100 eyes, 38 AD/76 eyes, Daping Hospital), 5-fold CV. Three-class MCI/AD/CN overall accuracy 91.64%, AUC 96.78%; 84.96% is the per-class PRECISION for MCI in that three-class model (80.90% is precision for the positive-cognitive-test group in a second, transfer-learning dataset).

quantity_a: Segment-level 10-fold cross-validated accuracy of a binary MCI vs HC classifier on resting-state EEG, N=61
quantity_b: Per-class precision (positive predictive value) for the MCI class within a three-class MCI/AD/CN classifier on retinal fundus + OCT images, eye-level 5-fold CV, N=117
incompatible_if_same: No. Accuracy and class-specific precision are different metrics, and the two are single cross-validated scores from unrelated methods; neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: binary MCI vs HC (P-117) vs three-class MCI/AD/CN (P-5)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: public Isfahan Noor Hospital EEG datasets vs Daping Hospital retinal cohort; record's dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (both internal CV, no external cohort) but different units (EEG segments vs eyes)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: EEG vs retinal imaging (fundus/OCT); no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: accuracy vs per-class precision; binary vs three-class
performance_validity: flag applies to P-117 on the source: 99.81% (and 99.51% full-channel) accuracy from internal 10-fold CV over segments of only 61 participants with no external cohort; the pack's performance_suspect=false arises only because the registry Best_Metric is 'not reported'. A performance comparison resting on P-117 cannot be genuine.
independence: Independent: different groups (King Saud University/NTNU vs Wenzhou/Daping), different cohorts and modalities.
grounds: P-117 reports binary MCI-vs-HC accuracy from resting-state EEG while P-5's 84.96% is the MCI-class precision of a three-class retinal-imaging model, so metric type, task and modality all differ.
The dataset-family and modality-family gates fail with no waiver on record.
P-117 itself meets the performance-validity exclusion (99.81% on internal CV of 61 participants, no external cohort), so the pair could not be a genuine performance conflict in any case.
The pack PDF for P-117 is the wrong paper (an MRI-PET fusion study); the verdict rests on the correct P-117 PDF located in the repository.

With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method. (correct PDF)
For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets (correct PDF)
divided into 3660 segments (1740 segments from MCI cases and 1860 from HC cases) (correct PDF)
taken from Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) online dataset (pack PDF pdf/P-117.txt: the MRI-PET fusion paper, the wrong document)
The proposed method achieved high precision rates of 84.96% and 80.90% in classifying MCI and positive test scores for cognitive impairment, respectively.
The first dataset included information for a total of 29 patients (58 eyes) with MCI, 50 age-matched individuals with CN (100 eyes), and 38 patients (76 eyes) with AD.
As shown in Table 2, the proposed network DuCAN had an accuracy of 91.64% and an AUC of 96.78%.

record_defects: The pack/paper_pdf_map entry for P-117 ('formula-unverified') points to the wrong PDF (S1746809422007662, Rallabandi MRI-PET fusion); the correct P-117 PDF is S1746809423008959 (summaries.md header S1746809423005462 does not exist in downloads).
claim_b 'P-5: 84.96% precision on T1' mislabels the task: the figure is MCI-class precision within a three-class MCI/AD/CN model.
dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong (separate Iranian EEG and Chinese retinal cohorts); validation_comparable='Yes' ignores segment-level vs eye-level CV.
gap_magnitude 0.149 subtracts a precision from an accuracy.
The bridging-evidence list (P-360, P-322, P-324, P-387 'Left P100 latency') explains nothing about this pair.
C-49 is an exact duplicate of this record (same pair after the P-10 -> P-5 repoint).
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these documents; the pair shares neither modality, cohort, task nor metric.
